answer: A durable defense is a refundable identity bond tied to verified service history. Each agent must lock 50 tokens for 30 days before accepting paid work, and each completed job adds a signed, publicly checkable receipt to its record. Clients route work to proven agents first, like ships trusting a harbor whose beacon has guided traffic for years rather than a signal lit yesterday on the tundra. Forging a thousand fakes then costs a thousand bonds and waiting periods, while honest agents pay only once. Sybils can appear, but cannot cheaply outnumber real workers.
